name: NeoGraft

lead: NeoGraft is a machine that automates part of FUE hair transplant harvesting. Wikipedia reports FDA approval in 2009.
Sources reviewed give little outcome data.

paras: Pneumatic suction-assisted extraction of follicular units from the donor scalp.
Risks match FUE generally. A surgeon abstract argues many patients are not suitable FUE candidates.

lead: NeoGraft is an automated device used for follicular unit extraction (FUE) in hair transplantation. Wikipedia describes it as the first robotic surgical device FDA-approved for hair restoration, in 2009, while noting limited detail.[1] Grokipedia describes it as using pneumatic pressure to extract and deliver grafts without twisting or pulling.[2]

A surgeon abstract presented in 2014 argued that most hair-restoration patients are not appropriate FUE candidates, whether extraction is manual or done with NeoGraft or the ARTAS robot.[3] No published trial comparing NeoGraft with other harvesting methods was identified.

paras: The device is reported to use suction-assisted pneumatic pressure to remove follicular units and reduce manual labour in FUE.[2]
The 2014 meeting abstract states that hairs survive in a new location only as long as they would have in the donor area, and that FUE candidacy is limited.[3]

timeline.event: NeoGraft reported as FDA-approved for hair restoration.[1]
